note: Registry of record for the discovery tournament. The 30 entries are policy variants/mechanisms with documented overlaps (see known_risks and design.md section 11), not 30 independent paradigms. implementation_status is flipped from pending to implemented by each group task and must read implemented for all 30 before Phase 1 (test_registry_all_implemented).

methods.name: Greedy baseline (control)
methods.mechanism: Observed soft-field agreement count; sort by (-score, pair_key); take non-overlapping pairs; asks = baseline_asks. Byte-identical to policy.py --baseline greedy.
methods.computational_complexity: O(a^2) per match phase (a = available members)
methods.known_risks: Control reference: any divergence from policy.py corrupts every paired delta (test_m01_matches_control_greedy).
methods.literature_inspiration: Validated greedy implementation in this repository (kit.baseline_match).

methods.name: Reciprocal sum
methods.mechanism: directional(a,b) = sum over SOFT fields a observed of (1 equal / 0 unequal / prior 1/|OPTIONS[k]| when b missing); score = d(a,b) + d(b,a); greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Collapses to 2x match-count when both sides fully observed; differentiation driven by missing fields and asked values.
methods.literature_inspiration: Reciprocal recommender bilateral fusion (sum aggregation of directional preferences).

methods.name: Reciprocal minimum
methods.mechanism: score = min(d(a,b), d(b,a)) with the same directional as m02; greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Weakest-side rule can starve asymmetric-coverage members; coarse ties on low-coverage pools.
methods.literature_inspiration: Weakest-side reciprocity (bilateral min fusion in reciprocal recommendation).

methods.name: Reciprocal product
methods.mechanism: score = d(a,b) * d(b,a); greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Zero when either direction has no observed overlap; may reduce introductions on cold_start.
methods.literature_inspiration: Mutual scoring via product of directional preferences (bilateral compatibility).

methods.name: Harmonic reciprocal score
methods.mechanism: score = 2*d(a,b)*d(b,a)/(d(a,b)+d(b,a)), 0 when the sum is 0; greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Rank correlates strongly with m04 (flagged as partial redundancy for retention diagnostics).
methods.literature_inspiration: Harmonic-mean aggregation for symmetric fit (penalizes asymmetry).

methods.name: Bottleneck compatibility
methods.mechanism: score = min over the 4 REL fields of (1 equal / 0 unequal when both observed, prior 1/|OPTIONS[k]| when either missing); greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Only REL fields decide rank; coarse ties when REL coverage is low.
methods.literature_inspiration: Weakest-link / bottleneck compatibility (prioritizing the weakest important dimension).

methods.name: Prune-and-greedy
methods.mechanism: Drop candidate pairs whose observed soft agreement is below PRUNE_MIN_SCORE=2, then greedy take on survivors using base score.
methods.known_risks: Cutoff constant frozen pre-tournament; may reduce introductions when coverage is sparse.
methods.literature_inspiration: Prune-and-greedy (Gravin, Tang, Wang: pruned search heuristics for online matching).
methods.substituted_from: m07_match_count_symmetric: symmetric observed-soft count yields the identical ordering to greedy control by construction - honestly impossible to distinguish, replaced per spec Section 3.

methods.name: Weighted compatibility score
methods.mechanism: Static structure-only weights w_k = 1 - 1/|OPTIONS[k]| from kit.OPTIONS cardinalities; score = sum w_k*(1 equal / 0 unequal when both observed; w_k*p_k when exactly one observed; 0 both missing); greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Prior-fill terms may dominate ranking on cold_start (low coverage); no outcome fitting is used by design.
methods.literature_inspiration: Principled field-discrimination weighting; analogous to static thresholds derived from visible option distributions.

methods.name: Partner scarcity
methods.mechanism: score = base / max(1, min(deg_a, deg_b)) where deg = member's feasible degree in today's graph; rescues scarce members.
methods.known_risks: Degree distributions differ sharply per variant; may over-rescue on sparse.
methods.literature_inspiration: Degree-aware matching / scarce-partner preference in queueing with degree-aware admission.

methods.name: Degree-balanced matching
methods.mechanism: score = base / max(1, max(deg_a, deg_b)); penalizes consuming members who have many alternatives.
methods.known_risks: Opposite bias to m09; both may suppress total introductions (guardrail metrics report this).
methods.literature_inspiration: Opportunity-cost degree balancing (value members relative to outside options).

methods.name: Scarcity x compatibility
methods.mechanism: score = base * 2/(deg_a + deg_b); multiplicative product of pair quality with average scarcity.
methods.known_risks: Near-monotone with m09 in practice (flagged as redundancy risk for retention diagnostics).
methods.literature_inspiration: Scarcity-weighted quality scoring (product form).

methods.name: Regret score
methods.mechanism: score = base - max(0, alt_a - base) - max(0, alt_b - base) where alt_m = m's best other feasible edge score today.
methods.known_risks: Only the top alternative counts; many moderate options are ignored.
methods.literature_inspiration: Regret / opportunity-cost matching (waiting-loss accounting for both endpoints).

methods.name: Opportunity-cost score
methods.mechanism: score = base - max(gap_a, gap_b); conservative single-side second-best comparison.
methods.known_risks: Suppresses strong pairs when one endpoint has a strong alternative (may trade MSMI for coverage).
methods.literature_inspiration: Second-best alternative comparison (opportunity cost of consuming a member).

methods.name: Mutual regret
methods.mechanism: score = base - min(gap_a, gap_b); penalizes only when both endpoints have waiting alternatives.
methods.known_risks: Weak penalty when only one side is scarce; correlates with m13 on dense pools.
methods.literature_inspiration: Mutual (both-sides) opportunity-cost combination.

methods.name: Reserve high-option-value members
methods.mechanism: score = base - (cnt_a + cnt_b) where cnt_m = count of m's other feasible edges with base >= STRONG_SCORE=3.
methods.known_risks: Count-based rule overlaps m28 blocked-value accounting (flagged as redundancy risk).
methods.literature_inspiration: Reservation of high-option members (avoid consuming members with many strong alternatives).

methods.name: Patient policy
methods.mechanism: Wait when quality is weak: keep only pairs with base >= PATIENT_MIN_SCORE=3 (at least 3 of the 7 observed soft fields - the suite strong-alignment cutoff, same constant as STRONG_SCORE), then greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Adapted WITHOUT departure signals; Akbarpour et al. show patient wins require them - may idle too much (zero-selection days diagnose this).
methods.literature_inspiration: Patient vs greedy matching (Akbarpour, Eeckhout, Lerman, Milton, JPE 2020), adapted to a quality gate since exit_day is unobservable.

methods.name: Daily quota policy
methods.mechanism: Greedy take, then keep only the top ceil(n/QUOTA_DIVISOR) = ceil(n/2) selected pairs (QUOTA_DIVISOR=2); withheld pairs remain available for later days.
methods.known_risks: Half-throughput days interact badly with a fixed 60-day horizon if late days are thin.
methods.literature_inspiration: Batching / controlled clearing (Eom & Toriello 2026: batching and greedy near-optimal in two-sided matching).

methods.name: Time-dependent acceptance threshold
methods.mechanism: Gate: keep pairs with base >= max(1, TIME_T0 - day//TIME_STEP); equals 4 on days 0-19, 3 on 20-39, 2 on 40-59.
methods.known_risks: Late-horizon laxness may admit weak pairs; all constants frozen pre-tournament.
methods.literature_inspiration: Time-decreasing acceptance thresholds (dual/delay-cost threshold policies in online matching).

methods.name: Arrival-age policy
methods.mechanism: Greedy take ordered by primary key -max(wait_a, wait_b), then -base, then pair key: longest-waiting members matched first.
methods.known_risks: Priority may override strong pairs for old weak ones; reads only arrived_day (never exit_day).
methods.literature_inspiration: Fairness / FCFS arrival-age priority in matchmaking and queue admission.

methods.name: New-arrival protection
methods.mechanism: Filter out any pair where min(wait_a, wait_b) < PROTECT_DAYS=3; greedy take on the rest (new members accumulate alternatives first).
methods.known_risks: Three-day grace constant frozen; reduces early-horizon throughput.
methods.literature_inspiration: Exploration warm-up / new-arrival protection (bandit warm-up analogy).

methods.name: Delay-cost threshold
methods.mechanism: Per-pair gate: keep if base >= max(0, DELAY_T0 - max(wait_a, wait_b)//DELAY_STEP); 4 for waits 0-14, 3 for 15-29, 2 for 30-44, 1 for 45-59, 0 afterwards; then greedy take.
methods.known_risks: Wait time is only a statistical proxy for remaining availability, not real expiration data.
methods.literature_inspiration: Delay-cost threshold policies (Mari, Bernasconi, Baumann, Stoesser, Dilkina, AAMAS 2023).
methods.substituted_from: m21_expiration_aware: requires exit_day, which is a banned unobservable input (spec Section 9) - replaced per spec Section 3.

methods.name: Market-thickness policy
methods.mechanism: If today's average feasible degree 2E/V < THIN_AVG_DEG=2.0: match nothing (wait); otherwise full greedy.
methods.known_risks: Binary all-day gate can idle entire days at degree just under the cutoff; no partial response.
methods.literature_inspiration: Cost-balancing WHEN-to-match trigger (Liu, Zhang, Zhang, arXiv:2601.21858) and epsilon-proxy clearing (Kerimov et al.).

methods.name: Hybrid patient-greedy
methods.mechanism: Favorable if max base >= HYBRID_MIN_SCORE=4 OR avg degree >= HYBRID_AVG_DEG=3.0: full greedy; otherwise match nothing (wait).
methods.known_risks: OR-gate makes waiting rare (top score >= 4 happens most days); thresholds frozen pre-tournament.
methods.literature_inspiration: Conditional patience: greedy under favorable conditions, wait under low opportunity density (Akbarpour et al.; Costabal et al. WHEN-to-match).

methods.name: Maximum-cardinality-first matching
methods.mechanism: Cardinality first: exact Kuhn augmenting-path maximum matching on the bipartite 2-coloring of today's feasible graph (adjacency sorted by -base then pair key as secondary preference); non-bipartite graphs fall back to greedy take plus length-3 augmenting exchanges (documented approximation).
methods.computational_complexity: O(V*E) Kuhn per match phase; fallback O(E * rounds)
methods.known_risks: Odd-cycle graphs take the approximate fallback (measured reachable: 5/90 fixture snapshots; forced by odd-cycle tests); secondary score preference is heuristic (adjacency order only); fallback mechanism overlaps m27 (flagged).
methods.literature_inspiration: Maximum-cardinality bipartite matching (Kuhn/Hopcroft-Karp); cardinality-first allocation.

methods.name: Maximum-weight matching
methods.mechanism: Maximize total base-score weight: zero-score edges pruned (exact for value), Hungarian/Kuhn-Munkres O(n^3) when the graph is 2-colorable and node count <= HUNGARIAN_NODE_CAP=180; otherwise greedy take plus one-swap improvement (documented approximation).
methods.known_risks: Exact only for bipartite node count <= 180 (cap breaches measured reachable: 6/90 fixture snapshots); non-bipartite fallback shares logic with m26 (documented overlap); zero-score edge pruning leaves the weight objective exact but may reduce cardinality vs m24.
methods.literature_inspiration: Maximum-weight assignment (Kuhn-Munkres); prophet-style value-maximizing allocation (Ezra et al.).

methods.name: Greedy + one-swap improvement
methods.mechanism: Greedy take, then repeat improving pair exchanges: replace (a,b)+(c,d) with (a,d)+(c,b) or (a,c)+(b,d) when both replacements are feasible, non-past, non-overlapping and strictly increase total base weight; iterate to local optimum (integer weights guarantee termination).
methods.known_risks: Local optimum only; O(p^2) with p = matched pairs (latency-tested).
methods.literature_inspiration: Two-exchange local search on matchings (classic matching local improvement).

methods.name: Greedy + augmenting-path improvement
methods.mechanism: Greedy take, then short augmenting exchanges of length <= 3: if (x,x') is matched and free y adjacent to x and free z adjacent to x' exist with feasible edges, replace with (x',z)+(x,y), gaining +1 cardinality; loop until no gain (cap AUGMENT_ROUNDS_CAP=50).
methods.known_risks: Length-3 only: not exact maximum cardinality (that is m24); spirit overlaps m24's non-bipartite fallback.
methods.literature_inspiration: Berge augmenting paths; greedy + short augmenting exchange heuristics in online matching.

methods.name: Conflict-aware greedy
methods.mechanism: score = 3*base - pool_a - pool_b where pool_m = sum of base over all feasible edges incident to m (blocked-alternative value accounting; pools include the current pair).
methods.known_risks: Pool sums can dominate base on dense variants; ranking overlaps degree-based m09/m10 (flagged as redundancy risk).
methods.literature_inspiration: Conflict-aware greedy: adjust scores by the value of alternatives blocked by consuming both endpoints (auction/conflict heuristics).

methods.name: Uncertainty-aware policy
methods.mechanism: Active asking: hard-constraint asks first but capped to keep SOFT_ASK_RESERVE=3 budget units for soft fields; soft asks ranked by information value = number of incident feasible edges whose partner already has that field observed (immediately resolvable comparisons); ask highest value first, never declined fields. Match phase = baseline_match on the refreshed state.
methods.known_risks: Value counts only one-sided-resolvable edges; may under-ask when both sides miss the same field; SOFT_ASK_RESERVE trades one constraints bundle per day (3 vs the control's 4) for soft coverage - reported as secondary ask cost, never ranked.
methods.literature_inspiration: Active preference elicitation / match-sensitive active learning (Charlin et al., ICML 2012); bandit matching with costly interviews.

methods.name: Targeted information policy
methods.mechanism: VoI gate: hard-constraint asks first but capped to keep SOFT_ASK_RESERVE=3 budget units; then for each soft candidate (available member with unobserved non-declined field, sorted by member_id, field): enumerate kit.OPTIONS[k] truth-blind and ask only if at least one option changes today's greedy allocation (incident-edge score recomputation + greedy_take); budget-bounded. Match phase = baseline_match on the refreshed state.
methods.computational_complexity: O(c * |OPTIONS| * (deg + E log E)) VoI gate, c = soft candidates evaluated
methods.known_risks: Up to |OPTIONS| greedy passes per candidate, hard-capped at VOI_EVAL_CAP=96 recomputations per ask phase in fixed enumeration order (worst-case fixture-tested); measured workload <= ~800 soft-not-asked pairs/day on <= 18-edge graphs; SOFT_ASK_RESERVE trades one constraints bundle per day (3 vs 4); gate compares allocations, never truth.
methods.literature_inspiration: Value-of-information targeted clarification (VoI gate pattern validated in research/e3_rel_experiment E1); active learning without hidden state.
